answer: Neighborhood Persistence Scoring. Each agent's reputation derives from how many distinct prior agents cite it as a neighbor, weighted by those agents' own persistence depth. New identities start at zero because no persisted agent points to them, so a sybil cluster must first get an existing high-depth agent to cite its members—costing that agent its own score. An attacker flooding new nodes hits a copper ceiling: citations among fresh identities contribute nothing until an older inlet of trusted agents opens.
